title: Volume 9 · Malaysian Tax and Statutory Setup
subtitle: Lessons 1–4: SST templates that survive an audit, item tax categories that match the law, and an SST-02 return that reconciles
outcomes: Build sales and purchase tax templates with separate liability accounts
Map items to tax categories so the right rate lands on the right line
Produce SST-02 figures that tie to the general ledger
Handle exempt and zero-rated lines with the evidence an auditor asks for

slides.title: Build the SST templates an auditor expects
bullets: One template per rate per direction: sales tax out, service tax out, purchase tax in
Each template names an account, and those accounts become the return's source lines
Service tax on services is eight per cent, sales tax on goods is ten per cent in our sample
Never reuse one account for both output and input, or the return cannot be split

rows: Service Tax 8 %, account Service Tax Output - SM
Purchase tax 10 % and service tax 8 %, input accounts

slides.notes: Separate accounts are the whole trick: output tax is a liability, input tax is an asset, and the difference is what you file. Most Malaysian sites start with one combined account and then cannot produce SST-02 without a spreadsheet. Fix it at configuration time, because changing it later means remapping every historical posting.

slides.title: One invoice that proves the matrix
bullets: Goods at ten per cent and services at eight per cent must sit on separate templates
The invoice total is net plus tax, and the tax amount is never income
Each tax row names its account, so the ledger carries the split automatically
An exempt line carries no tax but still needs a category for reporting

rows: General Ledger, Service Tax Output - SM

slides.notes: Two rates on one invoice is the case that breaks most first attempts, because a single template cannot carry both. Make the learner compute two thousand four hundred plus five hundred plus two hundred forty plus forty, and then read the same four numbers off the tax summary. When they agree, the tax configuration is defensible.

slides.title: Map items so the rate follows the product
bullets: Tax category on the item overrides the customer's default, and that precedence must be intended
A service item with sales tax creates an incorrect return even though the invoice looks right
Exempt goods need their own category and a reason code, not just a zero rate
Review the mapping once with the client's tax advisor and keep the email

rows: Tax section, item tax template Sales Tax 10 %
Exempt packaging with the exempt category
One line each of the three items

slides.notes: Precedence confuses everyone, so write it on the configuration worksheet: item template beats customer template beats company default. Test it with the three-line invoice above and the client can see the precedence rather than being told about it. When the tax advisor changes a rate, this is also the list you update.

slides.title: Produce SST-02 figures from the ledger
bullets: The return is built from posted invoices, so drafts and cancelled documents must be excluded
Output tax total equals the credit balance on the output accounts for the period
Input tax is only claimable on invoices that are submitted and matched to a receipt
The payable figure is output minus input, and it must tie to the ledger to the cent

rows: SST Output and SST Input balances
Return reference in the tax worksheet

slides.notes: Twelve hundred out, one hundred twenty in, one thousand eighty payable: three numbers that must appear in the report, in the ledger and on the return. If they do not, the usual causes are a draft invoice counted, a credit note not reversing tax, or a purchase invoice without the input template. All three are visible in the tax summary by account.

slides.title: Three numbers that must agree
bullets: The return figure, the tax summary and the ledger balance are the same number seen three ways
A draft or cancelled document in the summary shifts the return and must be explained
Input tax is only claimable where the purchase invoice exists, so unbooked bills understate the claim
Sign the worksheet with the date filed, because that is the audit evidence

rows: Your own arithmetic and the return

slides.notes: The check takes four minutes and prevents the most common compliance finding: a return that disagrees with the ledger because a document was posted in a later period. Print the summary for the period, print the ledger for the same accounts, and staple them to the return. When an auditor asks, the answer is a page rather than an explanation.

slides.title: Exempt and zero-rated lines with evidence
bullets: An exemption is a category plus a certificate, not a zero typed into a rate field
Schedule A and B exemptions must be referenced on the invoice or the claim fails
Exempt sales still appear in the return, in their own box
Keep the customer's exemption certificate with the customer record

rows: 0 % with the Exempt - SM account mapping
Exemption certificate number in the customer record

slides.notes: Exemptions are where clients get enthusiastic and auditors get interested, so the rule is one certificate per customer, stored, with an expiry date. The system will happily apply a zero rate; it cannot judge whether the exemption is valid. Put that judgement in writing and attach it to the customer record before the first exempt invoice.

slides.title: Malaysian configuration checklist
bullets: Tax rates, accounts and categories are configuration, and they must be evidenced
e-Invoice readiness depends on the same master data being clean
Every row below has an owner in the client's finance team
Revisit annually, because rates and thresholds change with each budget

rows: 10 per cent to SST Output - SM
8 per cent to Service Tax Output - SM
10 per cent and 8 per cent input accounts

slides.notes: This checklist is the deliverable that makes a compliance conversation concrete. Hand it over signed, with the tax advisor's email attached, and the client's auditor has a starting point that is not a memory of a phone call. It also protects the consultant when a rate changes and nobody told them.

slides.title: Reading the tax summary by account
bullets: Grouping by account is what makes the return auditable, because each account is one box
A single blended tax account hides the split between sales tax and service tax
Credit notes must reduce both the taxable amount and the tax in the same period
Compare the summary with the general ledger, not with a spreadsheet

rows: General Ledger for the same accounts

slides.notes: Twelve hundred of sales tax plus forty of service tax less one hundred twenty of input is one thousand one hundred twenty payable, and that single sum is what the client actually pays. Show the arithmetic in the meeting rather than the report, because the sum is what gets remembered and the report is what gets filed.

lab.title: Lab · Build SST templates, map an item mix and reconcile the return
steps: Create sales tax at 10 per cent and service tax at 8 per cent with separate output accounts
Create the matching input templates on the purchase side
Attach item tax templates to the blender, the delivery service and the exempt carton
Raise a mixed invoice with all three lines and confirm 240.00, 40.00 and 0.00
Confirm the invoice total of 2,940.00 with 280.00 of tax
Produce the January tax summary and confirm 1,200.00 output and 120.00 input
Compute the net payable and tie it to the two ledger accounts
Attach an exemption certificate to a customer and invoice an exempt line
lab.done: Done when the tax summary and the ledger agree on output and input, the mixed invoice shows both rates correctly, and the exempt customer has a stored certificate.

quiz.question: Why keep separate accounts for sales tax and service tax output?
options: Because the return needs each box separately
quiz.why: SST-02 reports sales tax and service tax in different boxes, so they need separate accounts; a blended account cannot be split later.

quiz.question: Which document beats which when deciding an item's tax rate?
quiz.why: Precedence runs from the most specific to the least: item tax template, then customer or supplier template, then company default.

quiz.question: Output tax of 1,200.00 and input tax of 120.00 give a payable of what?
quiz.why: The payable is output minus input, 1,200.00 − 120.00 = 1,080.00, and it must tie to the two ledger balances.

quiz.question: What makes an exempt sale defensible?
options: A category plus a stored exemption certificate
quiz.why: An exemption needs a category for reporting and a certificate as evidence; a zero rate alone gives the auditor nothing to test.

quiz.question: Which documents must be excluded from the SST return?
quiz.why: Only posted, submitted documents carry tax liability. Drafts have not happened and cancelled documents have been reversed.

memory.spine: One tax template per rate per direction, an item category that follows the product, and a return that is the ledger seen three ways.

device.label: One template per rate per direction
expansion: Sales tax out, service tax out and purchase tax in never share a template
Goods at ten per cent and services at eight per cent sit on separate lines and templates
Item tax category overrides the customer default, which must be intended rather than discovered
SST-02 comes from posted invoices, so drafts and cancellations are excluded
The return, the tax summary and the ledger are one number seen three ways

cards.q: Why one template per rate per direction?
cards.a: The posting account and the return box differ by direction, and mixing them makes the return untraceable.

cards.q: Goods at ten per cent and services at eight per cent on one invoice?
cards.a: Two lines on two templates, each rate posting to its own account.

cards.q: Item tax category or customer default, which applies?
cards.a: The item's category wins, which is useful for exempt goods and dangerous when unintended.

cards.q: Which documents feed the SST-02 return?
cards.a: Posted invoices only, because drafts, cancelled documents and unsubmitted returns are excluded.
The return figure, the tax summary by account and the ledger balance of the tax account.

trap.what: An exempt customer is handled by typing zero per cent into the rate field.
trap.why: No exemption category or certificate sits behind the zero, so the return cannot evidence why tax was not charged.

narration: Malaysian tax is the part clients test you on first, because the numbers go to a government portal. Build separate templates for sales tax and service tax, with separate output and input accounts, because the return needs each box separately. Attach item tax templates so the rate follows the product: ten per cent goods, eight per cent services, zero for exempt with a stored certificate. Then the return: twelve hundred output less one hundred twenty input is one thousand eighty payable, and the same three numbers must appear in the tax summary, the ledger and the form. If they do not, the cause is a draft counted, a credit note that did not reverse tax, or a purchase without an input template. Keep the tax advisor's written confirmation with the configuration worksheet, because rates and thresholds change with every budget, and the consultant who documented the basis is the one who gets called back rather than blamed.
